parole.testo: From dialectal (Cham) fal, from Vulgar Latin *fallia, deverbal of Latin fallere; compare French faille (“fault”), Italian faglia (“fault”), Aromanian fai f (“fault, sin”). Less likely from Gothic 𐍆𐌰𐌹𐌰𐌽 (faian, “to blame”).
Possibly Italian fango from borrowed from Vulgar Latin *fangus (“mud”). Jokl claims a borrowing from Gothic 𐍅𐌰𐌲𐌲𐍃 (waggs, “paradise, *meadow”), from Proto-Germanic *wangaz (“field, meadow”).
